note: AutoTone clips 1% at each end of the luma histogram instead of 0.1%, so a clean ramp gets a black point above 0, caught by AutoToneTests.rampIsIdentity
AutoTone averages an empty bright set, so an all-black buffer's white balance is NaN, caught by AutoToneTests.blackSuggestsIdentity
AutoTone inverts the levels gamma ratio, so a median at a quarter of the span gets gamma 0.5 instead of 2, caught by AutoToneTests.levelsStretchAndCentreMedian
AutoTone white balance keeps pixels with a channel at 0 or 1, so clamped bright highlights skew the balance, caught by AutoToneTests.clippedHighlightsIgnored
anchor: guard rgb.min() > 0, rgb.max() < 1 else { return nil }

note: AutoTone white balance averages every pixel instead of the brightest 5%, so a warm highlight over a cool picture is not neutralised, caught by AutoToneTests.balanceReadsBrightestFivePercent
AutoTone white balance drops the slider clamp, so an extreme cast suggests a temperature past -100 that whiteBalance refuses, caught by AutoToneTests.extremeCastClampsToSliderRange
AutoTone white balance drops only the tint slider clamp, so a strong green cast suggests tint 400 that whiteBalance refuses, caught by AutoToneTests.extremeTintClampsToSliderRange
AutoTone white balance averages the whole boundary luma bin instead of only the brightest pixels the bright set needs, caught by AutoToneTests.histogramBalanceMatchesFullSort
AutoTone drops the gamma cap, so a median almost on the black point suggests gamma 11.7 instead of 10, caught by AutoToneTests.gammaClampsToTen
AutoTone drops the minimumSpan guard, so a narrow-range image is stretched to 0...1 instead of keeping identity levels, caught by AutoToneTests.narrowRangeKeepsIdentityLevels
anchor: white - black >= minimumSpan else { return tone }

note: AutoTone reads the levels histogram before the white balance instead of after it, so a tinted ramp gets the unbalanced points, caught by AutoToneTests.levelsReadAfterWhiteBalance
